title: Rodent Brain Extraction and Dissection: A Comprehensive Approach
author: Aboghazleh, Boyajian, et al.

steps.title: Sedate and anesthetize rat
steps.instruction: Place the male rat in an isoflurane induction chamber (2–4 % for 2–4 min); then inject ketamine (80 mg/kg) and xylazine (10 mg/kg) intraperitoneally to achieve deep anesthesia. Alternatively, inject pentobarbital (50 mg/kg IP) instead of ketamine/xylazine.

substeps.instruction: Induce sedation with isoflurane 2–4 % for 2–4 min
Inject ketamine 80 mg/kg and xylazine 10 mg/kg IP (or pentobarbital 50 mg/kg IP)

steps.title: Confirm deep anesthesia
steps.instruction: Return the rat to its cage and, every ~3 min, assess the absence of the toe‑pinch reflex; if the reflex persists, give an additional half dose of ketamine intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Decapitate and remove head
steps.instruction: Insert the rat’s head and the initial portion of its neck into the decapitator, then remove the head together with approximately 1 cm of neck.

steps.title: Incise scalp and retract
steps.instruction: Using a straight scissor, cut the scalp from the midline backward to forward; grasp each half with Halsted‑mosquito forceps and retract to expose the skull.

steps.title: Remove temporalis muscles
steps.instruction: Cut and remove the temporalis muscles on both sides of the skull with a surgical blade, exposing the temporal bones.

steps.title: Detach neck vertebrae and posterior muscles
steps.instruction: Cut the proximal neck and vertebrae from the occipital bone with a surgical blade or straight scissor; then remove remaining posterior and inferior skull muscles using forceps, a Boehler bone cutter, and serrated forceps.

steps.title: Cut mandible processes
steps.instruction: Using the Boehler bone cutter, cut the zygomatic arches, coronoid process, and angular process of the mandible on each side.

steps.title: Excise tympanic bullae
steps.instruction: Create a small window in the inferolateral skull by grasping and extracting each tympanic bulla with serrated forceps or the Boehler bone cutter.

steps.title: Remove occipital bone and expose brainstem
steps.instruction: Grasp the foramen magnum with the Boehler bone cutter, cut the occipital bone without damaging the spinal cord or brainstem, and remove it to expose the brainstem and cerebellum.

steps.title: Remove basal skull bones
steps.instruction: Using the Boehler bone cutter, cut and extract portions of the basal skull; insert <1 mm of the cutter tip between the lateral brain surface and the temporal bone and detach as much temporal bone as possible on each side, taking care not to press on the brain; then gently pull up the parietal bones from the posterior side and remove them together with remaining temporal bone.

steps.title: Trim frontal bone to expose olfactory bulbs
steps.instruction: Insert <1 mm of the Boehler cutter tip between the frontal bone and underlying cortex, and trim the frontal bone until the olfactory bulbs become visible.

steps.title: Cut cranial nerves and release brain
steps.instruction: On the inferior brain surface, cut the trigeminal and optic nerves; then separate the olfactory bulbs with a laboratory spatula or microscissor, freeing the brain for extraction.

steps.title: Prepare dissection station
steps.instruction: Clean ice packs, dissecting microscope, and all equipment with 70 % ethanol; keep the rat brain, dissection tools, and microscope stage on ice packs; place a petri dish on the ice and position the brain ventral side down in the dish.

steps.title: Midsagittal brain hemispheric cut
steps.instruction: Under the dissecting microscope, align a razor blade at the frontal and brainstem midsagittal planes, steady the brain with the left hand, and move the blade front‑to‑back until it contacts the petri dish, dividing the brain into right and left hemispheres.

steps.title: Rinse and dry hemispheres
steps.instruction: Apply normal saline or ACSF to aid separation of the hemispheres, discard excess solution, and wipe residual fluid with a swab.

steps.title: Isolate cerebellum from left hemisphere
steps.instruction: Flip the left hemisphere so the lateral side faces the petri dish; using a pointed curved tweezer in the left hand and a probe in the right hand, gently separate the cerebellum from the colliculi, pons, and medulla without rupturing any structures; transfer the cerebellum to a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Isolate hippocampus
steps.instruction: The hippocampus lies ~10 mm posterior to the brain tip. Starting at the posterior midline (anterior to the removed cerebellum), lift the cortex with the pointed curved tweezer while the probe separates it, exposing the white corpus callosum and the underlying C‑shaped hippocampus; carefully isolate the hippocampus without rupture, remove any attached cortex, and place it in a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Extract thalamus
steps.instruction: Medial and inferior to the hippocampus, ~8 mm from the brain tip, locate the oval thalamus bounded anteriorly by the fornix; using the probe (right hand) and tweezer (left hand) extract the thalamus and transfer it to a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Isolate corpus striatum
steps.instruction: Place a ruler under the petri dish; set the brain tip at 0 mm (excluding olfactory bulbs); measure 3 mm anteriorly and cut with a razor blade; then measure an additional 2 mm and make a second cut, yielding a 2 mm segment containing the corpus striatum (darker, drop‑like); isolate the striatum with the probe, avoiding the overlying corpus callosum, and place it in a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Isolate medial prefrontal cortex
steps.instruction: The medial prefrontal cortex spans 0.4–1 mm lateral from the midline and 1–4 mm from the brain tip; it can be taken from the first 3 mm frontal segment; isolate this small midline area between the forceps minor of the corpus callosum and the ventral orbital cortex, then transfer to a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Isolate brainstem
steps.instruction: Place the probe in front of the superior colliculus and behind the cortex; with the left hand steadying the brain, cut obliquely from anterior to the superior colliculus down to the pituitary gland, then move the probe downward to separate the brainstem from the remaining tissue; transfer the brainstem to a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Collect remaining cortical tissue
steps.instruction: From the remaining pieces (corpus striatum and medial prefrontal cortex extracts), take the uppermost external cortical tissue excluding the corpus callosum and also the cortex surrounding the hippocampus; place all collected cortex in a sterile, labeled Eppendorf tube.
